  }
  function updateDynoUI() {
    if(!ui)return;
    const busy=!!dyno?.busy,ready=!!(dynoEnabled && supported && dyno?.canUse() && !document.hidden && document.hasFocus());
    const context=ready&&!busy?dyno?.syncContext?.():null;
    if(context?.invalidated)dynoText='Car tuning or installed parts changed. Load settings or find a new tune for this game mode.';
    else if(context?.changed)dynoText=dyno.applied?'Applied tune found for this car and mode. Restore is available while it stays unchanged.':dyno.outcome?'Preview found for this car and mode. Review it before Apply.':'Ready for the selected mode. Load all settings or search a measured native estimate.';
    ui.querySelector('#dyno-mode').textContent=context?`Game tuning slot ${context.kind+1} of 5${Tune?.MODE_LABELS?.[context.kind]?' · '+Tune.MODE_LABELS[context.kind]:''} · selected in Mode Select`:busy&&dyno?.context?`Game tuning slot ${dyno.context.kind+1} of 5`:'Choose a race mode in the game, then open the Dyno main screen.';
    ui.querySelector('#dyno-find').disabled=!ready || busy || !!dyno?.applied;
    ui.querySelector('#dyno-cancel').disabled=!busy;
    ui.querySelector('#dyno-apply').disabled=!ready || busy || !(dyno?.full?dyno.outcome?.changed:dyno?.outcome?.improved) || !!dyno?.applied;
    ui.querySelector('#dyno-restore').disabled=!ready || busy || !dyno?.applied;
    ui.querySelector('#dyno-goal').disabled=busy;
    for(const option of ui.querySelector('#dyno-goal').options||[])if(['acceleration60','acceleration100','topSpeed'].includes(option.value))option.disabled=!dyno?.full;
    if(dyno && !dyno.full&&['acceleration60','acceleration100','topSpeed'].includes(ui.querySelector('#dyno-goal').value))ui.querySelector('#dyno-goal').value='peakPower';
    updateSetupEditor(ready,busy);
    ui.querySelector('#dyno-state').textContent=moduleFailure()?`Dyno unavailable. ${moduleFailure()}`:moduleProfile&&!moduleProfile.capabilities.dyno?'Not yet verified for this build':dynoText;
  }
  const tuneValue=value=>(value>100?'+':'')+(value-100);
  function updateSetupEditor(ready,busy){
    const editor=dyno?.editor,editable=!!(ready&&!busy&&editor&&!dyno?.applied);
    ui.querySelector('#tune-load').disabled=!ready||busy||!!dyno?.applied||!dyno?.full;
    ui.querySelector('#tune-preview').disabled=!editable;
    ui.querySelector('#tune-reset').disabled=!editable;
    ui.querySelector('#tune-group').disabled=!editable;
    const group=Tune?.GROUPS?.find(g=>g.id===ui.querySelector('#tune-group').value)||Tune?.GROUPS?.[0];
    for(let i=0;i<9;i++){
      const offset=group?.offsets[i],present=!!editor&&offset!==undefined,row=ui.querySelector('#tune-row-'+i),input=ui.querySelector('#tune-input-'+i);
      row.hidden=!present;input.disabled=!editable||!editor?.allowedOffsets.includes(offset);
      if(present){
        input.dataset.offset=String(offset);input.value=editor.draft[offset]-100;
        ui.querySelector('#tune-label-'+i).textContent=(Tune?.FIELD_LABELS?.[offset]||'Setting '+(offset+1))+(editor.allowedOffsets.includes(offset)?'':editor.unlockedOffsets?.includes(offset)?' · unverified':' · locked');
        ui.querySelector('#tune-value-'+i).textContent=tuneValue(editor.draft[offset]);
      }
    }
    const o=dyno?.outcome;
    ui.querySelector('#tune-changes').textContent=dyno?.full&&Array.isArray(o?.changes)?o.changes.map(x=>`${Tune?.FIELD_LABELS?.[x.offset]||x.field}: ${tuneValue(x.before)} → ${tuneValue(x.after)}${x.adjusted?' (native adjusted request '+tuneValue(x.requested)+')':''}`).join('\n')||'No accepted setup changes.':editor?'Edit sliders, then Preview changes. Drafts never alter the game.':'Load settings to see unlocked controls for this car and preset.';
  }
  async function runDyno(action) {
    if(!dynoEnabled || !dyno || dyno.busy)return;
    recordDiagnostic('dyno-action',{reason:action,tools:diagnosticTools()});
    suspend();
    dyno.setEnabled(true);
    try {
      if(action==='load'){
        await dyno.loadSetup();dynoText='All supported settings loaded. Edit a category, then Preview. Nothing changes in the game until Stage.';
      } else if(action==='preview'){
        const r=await dyno.preview();
        dynoText=`${r.changed?'Preview ready. Review accepted changes, then Stage selected preset.':'No accepted setup changes.'} Game unchanged. Native estimates: 0–60 ${r.bestResult.zeroTo60Seconds.toFixed(2)} s; 0–100 ${r.bestResult.zeroTo100Seconds.toFixed(2)} s; top ${(r.bestResult.topSpeedMps*3.6).toFixed(1)} km/h; ${r.bestResult.peakPowerKw.toFixed(1)} kW / ${r.bestResult.peakTorqueNm.toFixed(1)} Nm. NOS ${r.bestResult.nitrousSeconds.toFixed(2)} s / torque setting ${r.bestResult.nitrousTorque.toFixed(3)}. No handling/lap-time measurement.`;
      } else if(action==='find') {
        dynoText=dyno.full?'Searching in private memory · game setup stays unchanged':'Searching · original setup is restored after each trial';updateDynoUI();
        const r=await dyno.find({goal:ui.querySelector('#dyno-goal').value,onProgress:p=>{dynoText=`Searching ${p.evaluations}/${p.budget} trials · Cancel or F9 to stop`;updateDynoUI();}});
        const [field,unit]=({peakPower:['peakPowerKw','kW'],peakTorque:['peakTorqueNm','Nm'],acceleration60:['zeroTo60Seconds','s (0–60)'],acceleration100:['zeroTo100Seconds','s (0–100)'],topSpeed:['topSpeedMps','m/s']}[r.goal]);
        if(dyno.full){
          const manualSeed=r.seed?.some((value,index)=>value!==r.baseline[index]);
          const seedText=manualSeed&&r.changed?(r.improvedFromSeed?' Search improved the measured goal over your draft.':' No further measured improvement over the draft. Accepted manual draft retained.'):'';
          dynoText=`${r.baselineResult[field].toFixed(1)} → ${r.bestResult[field].toFixed(1)} ${unit} · ${r.evaluations} trials. Original kept. ${r.improved?'Measured goal improved versus original.':'No measured goal improvement versus original.'}${seedText} ${r.changed?'Review accepted changes, then Stage selected preset.':'No accepted setup changes.'} No handling/lap-time measurement.`;
        }else dynoText=`${r.baselineResult[field].toFixed(1)} → ${r.bestResult[field].toFixed(1)} ${unit} · ${r.evaluations} trials. Original kept. ${r.improved?'Stage preview to use this tune.':'No improvement found.'}`;
      } else if(action==='apply') {const r=await dyno.apply();dynoText=dyno.full?'Selected preset staged. Use the game’s Test Run to refresh driving physics, and Save Profile to persist. Disk save is not confirmed.'+(r.saveReady?'':' Other presets also have unsaved edits; native Save Profile saves them too.'):'Best tune applied. Use native Save Profile to persist.';}
      else {await dyno.restore();dynoText=dyno.full?'Previous current and selected-visit settings restored. Test Run refreshes physics. Save Profile again if you want this restored version persisted.':'Previous tune restored and confirmed.';}
    } catch(error) {recordDiagnostic('dyno-error',{error,dynoStatus:error?.dynoStatus,dynoGuard:error?.dynoGuard,dynoObserved:error?.dynoObserved,tools:diagnosticTools()});dynoText=error?.message || 'Dyno tuner stopped. Reload before retrying.';}
    updateDynoUI();
  }
  function exportDiagnostic() {
    if(!diagnostics){message('Diagnostic logger is unavailable. The game’s Download log may still have crash details.');return;}
    let url=null,link=null;
    try {
      recordDiagnostic('export',{tools:diagnosticTools()});
      const blob=new Blob([diagnostics.exportText()],{type:'application/json'});
      url=URL.createObjectURL(blob);link=document.createElement('a');link.href=url;link.download='nfsu2-driving-tools-diagnostics.json';link.hidden=true;
      (document.body||document.documentElement).append(link);link.click();
      message('Diagnostic download requested. It stays local until you choose to share the file. For native crash details, also use the game’s Download log.');
    } catch(error) {recordDiagnostic('engine-error',{error});message('Diagnostic download failed. Try again, or use the game’s Download log.');}
    finally {link?.remove();if(url)setTimeout(()=>URL.revokeObjectURL(url),1000);}
  }

    ui.querySelector('#hazards').hidden=!prefs.tester;
  }
  const profileLocks=()=>typeof navigator!=='undefined'&&navigator.locks&&typeof navigator.locks.request==='function'?navigator.locks:null;

  function selectProfile(){

  }
  function applyToolProfile(result,automatic=false){
    stopHostedSession('Profile Load stopped the hosted session. Press Start again.');
    if(driftPending)throw Error('Wait for the current drift request to confirm or time out, then Load again. No profile was loaded.');
    if(dyno?.busy||dyno?.pending){dyno.cancel();throw Error('Tuner cancellation requested. Wait for the pending game request to finish, then Load again. A staged preset is not reverted.');}
    clearRaceOnlyAI();
    adaptiveRaceEnabled=false;if(ui)ui.querySelector('#adaptive-race').checked=false;
    suspend();driftNeedsReapply=false;dragTakenOver=false;lastShift=0;lastPulse=0;
    const choices=result.settings;
    for(const key of Object.keys(prefs))prefs[key]=choices[key];
    dynoEnabled=choices.dynoEnabled;dyno?.setEnabled(dynoEnabled);
    if(ui){ui.querySelector('#dyno-goal').value=choices.dynoGoal;ui.querySelector('#profile-network').checked=result.profile.networkConsent;ui.querySelector('#profile-name').value=result.profile.name;}
    driftNeedsReapply=typeof prefs.drift==='boolean';profileDriftChoice=driftNeedsReapply;
    loadedProfile={id:result.profile.id,revision:result.profile.revision};savePrefs();syncProfileControls();
    dynoText=dynoEnabled?'Profile loaded. Open the solo Performance Tuning main screen. Existing staged presets are unchanged.':'Tuner off. Existing staged presets are unchanged.';updateDynoUI();
    profileNotice=(automatic?'Loaded on startup: ':'Loaded: ')+result.profile.name+'. Choices wait for verified game contexts.'+(result.profile.networkConsent?' Saved network permission restored where selected.':' Network permission and online no-clip remain off.')+' Game presets and drafts are not saved or restored by profiles.';
    message(profileNotice);renderProfiles();
  }
  function profileAction(action){
    if(profileActionPending)return;
    const request={stopToken:profileStore?.snapshot().stopToken,selection:profileSelection?{...profileSelection}:null,name:ui.querySelector('#profile-name').value,networkConsent:ui.querySelector('#profile-network').checked===true,auto:ui.querySelector('#profile-auto').checked,settings:{...prefs,dynoEnabled,dynoGoal:ui.querySelector('#dyno-goal').value}};
    const epoch=profileActionEpoch;
    // localStorage has no atomic compare-and-swap. Serialize named-profile
    // writes across tabs with a browser-managed lock; Stop remains immediate
    // and its independent marker invalidates any stale startup authorization.
    const execute=()=>{
      if(epoch!==profileActionEpoch)return;
      if(action==='auto'){
        const latest=profileStore?.refresh();
        if(!latest?.available||latest.stopToken!==request.stopToken){profileNotice='Stop or profile storage changed while waiting. Select a profile and request startup loading again.';renderProfiles();return;}
      }
      performProfileAction(action,request);
    };
    if(action==='load'){stopHostedSession('Profile Load stopped the hosted session. Press Start again.');execute();return;}
    const locks=profileLocks();
    if(!locks){profileNotice='Profile editing needs browser storage locking, which is unavailable. No profile was changed.';renderProfiles();return;}
    profileActionPending=true;renderProfiles();
    try{
      const result=locks.request('nfsu2-driving-tools-profiles-v1-write',execute);
      if(result&&typeof result.then==='function')result.catch(()=>{if(epoch===profileActionEpoch)profileNotice='Could not lock profile storage. No profile change was confirmed.';}).finally(()=>{if(epoch===profileActionEpoch){profileActionPending=false;renderProfiles();}});
      else {profileActionPending=false;renderProfiles();}
    }catch{profileActionPending=false;profileNotice='Could not lock profile storage. No profile change was confirmed.';renderProfiles();}
  }
  function performProfileAction(action,request){
    const selected=request.selection;
    try{
      if(!profileStore)throw Error('Profiles are unavailable.');
      if(action==='save'||action==='update'){
        if(action==='update'&&!selected)throw Error('Select a saved profile first.');
        const saved=profileStore.save({id:action==='update'?selected.id:null,revision:action==='update'?selected.revision:null,name:request.name,settings:request.settings,networkConsent:request.networkConsent});
        profileSelection=saved;profileNotice='Saved '+saved.name+' locally in this browser. This profile will not load on startup until explicitly enabled.';
      }else if(action==='load'){
        if(!selected)throw Error('Select a saved profile first.');
        applyToolProfile(profileStore.load(selected.id,selected.revision));return;
      }else if(action==='delete'){
        if(!selected)throw Error('Select a saved profile first.');
        profileStore.remove(selected.id,selected.revision);profileSelection=null;ui.querySelector('#profile-name').value='';ui.querySelector('#profile-network').checked=false;profileNotice='Saved profile deleted. Current controls are unchanged; automatic loading for it is off.';
      }else if(action==='auto'){
        const enabled=request.auto;
        if(enabled&&!selected)throw Error('Select a saved profile first.');
        profileStore.setAuto(enabled?selected.id:null,enabled?selected.revision:null);
        if(enabled){
          // Clear the fallback latch only AFTER the requested saved revision was
          // authorized successfully; a stale/failed enable must not erase Stop.
          try{sessionStorage.removeItem(PROFILE_SESSION_STOP);if(sessionStorage.getItem(PROFILE_SESSION_STOP)==='1')throw Error();}
          catch{try{profileStore.setAuto(null);}catch{}throw Error('Cannot clear the Stop pause in this tab. Automatic loading remains blocked here; check storage before retrying.');}
          profileSessionStopped=false;
        }
        profileNotice=enabled?'Load on startup enabled for '+selected.name+'. Its saved choices, including separately saved network permission, will be requested after reload. F9 pauses this.':'Automatic profile loading is off. Current controls are unchanged.';
      }
    }catch(error){profileNotice=error.message||'Profile action failed. Nothing was loaded.';message(profileNotice);}
    renderProfiles();
  }

# Read-only city event catalog checkpoint

## Scope and authority

This isolated city-catalog candidate publishes every currently selected native `g_spot.s` row, at most160, rather than narrowing the list to the current car's spot. This is the current native event offering across the city, not every raw career race or every locked stage. A fresh exact nearby-host offer and a freshly revalidated selected native destination are both required for JOIN. A catalog row cannot acquire an offer proof, open/create a lobby, far-join, navigate, press Enter, or change the game.

The catalog fragment is authored WAT in `tools/hosted-catalog.cjs`. It calls no native functions and can write only to the pump's checked owned allocation. The original free-roam call runs once before the pump. Allocation, registration, sequence/epoch/heartbeat, Stop/rearm and final JOIN CAS semantics remain in place. This checkpoint adds no travel operations or AI hooks. Unsupported binaries and failed hosted transformation/compile retain reviewed v0.33 behavior.

Grounding: `research/event-destination-catalog/CATALOG-RESEARCH.md` and its exact function mapping. Only original hash `128e2b5816a8eace4b768aec920318a1613da8235801a361e2009e96550be1d6` is supported. Original game functions are used only in offline compile/preservation checks and the bounded synthetic fixture, never copied into the shipping profile.

## Mailbox v3

Registration kind and magic stay unchanged. Header version is3 and allocation size54736. The mandatory176-byte command proof begins at54560; see `integration/DESTINATION-PROOF.md`. Client requires matching profile version, size, and catalog schema and mandatory destination-proof schema before decoding. Existing fields/offers at0..703 stay at the same offsets.

-704 current native `mp_spot_here` trigger ID;708 marker hash. These extend `snapshot.spot` and do not extend offer authority.
-712 car ID;716 race-table ID;720/724 type13 trigger-span start/end;728 i64 native completed-sweep deadline. These are valid only when the catalog is valid. They identify this session/source, not persistent user-facing IDs.
-736..767 reserved.
-768 catalog version1;772 valid0/1;776 count;780 capacity160;784 row stride336;788 current stage;792 native refresh-in-progress0/1;796 reserved.
-800 begins160 fixed336-byte rows.

Each row has unsigned32 values except the explicitly typed fields:

|Offset|Field|
|---|---|
|0/4/8|Trigger ID / marker hash / event hash|
|12/16/20/24/28|First track / raw type / reverse / raw laps / race stage|
|32/36/40/44/48/52|Category / SUV boolean / heat count / native kind / native why / race table index|
|56/60/64|GPS approachXYZ, signed32 whole metres|

Snapshot fields: `catalog` is a deeply frozen array; aliases `catalogValid`, `catalogStage`, `catalogRefreshing` describe it. `catalogSnapshot` includes version, valid, count, capacity, stride, stage, refreshing, sequence, nativeNowBigInt, carId, raceTableId, triggerFirst, triggerEnd, sweepNextBigInt. Row fields are triggerId, markerHash, eventHash, track, rawType, reverse, laps, stage, category, suvRequired, heatCount, kind, why, raceIndex, route, marker, box, heats, nativeName, trackLabel, heading, triggerSize.

The shared snapshot seqlock brackets both legacy offers and catalog. Only immutable `offers` enter the private offer-proof WeakMap. The selector passes its exact intended destination/context to the client; the client compares them to a fresh native row and serializes only that row. Native dispatch revalidates current actual spot, full identity/geometry/restrictions/source context and the fresh offered race immediately before the final CAS. Localized names are display data, never identity.

## Validation and labels

Required data fails the entire catalog closed: every covered guest page including interior holes, host ranges, counts, race-table membership/stride, complete variable-size trigger chain and actual record boundaries, source stage/span consistency, completed native sweep, published row kinds/reasons, race type/category/stage/heats, marker-hash equality, finite ordered boxes, equality of copied and live trigger boxes, finite marker/heading values and unique trigger IDs. The in-progress `nw` array is never read. Distinct trigger records sharing a marker hash stay distinct. The native kind/why fields are copied, not recreated through progression mutations. No career-credit guarantee is exposed.

Kind1 is career-open, kind2 multiplayer-only. Why0 open;1 already won;2 not open yet;3 sign with sponsor;4 sponsor contract;5 opens after more wins;6 SUV required. Category2 is URL before raw type mapping. Other mapped raw types are0 Circuit,1 Sprint,2 Street X,4 Drag,5 Drift. Three bounded native heat tuples preserve URL identity; only the first heat's optional localized label is copied.

Native internal names use the source string-pool offset with a47-byte, terminated, printable-ASCII bound. Optional localized names require a known signed TrackInfo ID (count<=2000), a fully readable strictly hash-sorted text table (count<=200000), native bhash lookup with reverse-name-first fallback, and a terminated source of at most63 Latin-1 bytes. Controls are sanitized; printable Latin-1 becomes UTF8. Invalid/missing optional data becomes an empty label with honest `Track N` fallback. No names are invented, no native formatter is called, and text is never an action or permission.

Validation runs once per publication, not once per localized row. Synthetic worst-case160 rows and200000 text entries measured about0.326ms per snapshot over20 runs in the focused run. This is not a live-game performance result. No unsafe cache assumes same-address text tables are immutable; required data is reread each frame. A later optimization needs an independently established table generation/lifetime contract.

All execution was synthetic offline; original game bytes were compiled/preserved only. This catalog is a prerequisite for travel, not travel itself.

## Snapshot-contention review fix

The client now exposes a read-only `snapshotStatus` getter describing only the latest `snapshot()` attempt: `ready`, `busy`, `invalid`, or `unavailable`. Three odd/torn seqlock attempts produce `busy`. A payload-validation failure rechecks the snapshot sequence before classifying it: a changed/odd sequence discards that partial attempt, while malformed data under the same even sequence is immediately `invalid`. The busy path rechecks the immutable header and session, so invalid/replaced attachments do not receive contention grace. Missing registration or pending memory growth is `unavailable`. No coherent snapshot is cached by the client and no offer-proof checks were relaxed. Busy arm/heartbeat/JOIN attempts return false without writing a command, and a previous offer becomes unusable after publication changes its sequence.

The parent owns any bounded queue/UI grace for explicitly busy snapshots. Such grace must skip all actions, retain prior data only for display, require a new coherent snapshot before Start or JOIN, and stop on invalid/unavailable or grace expiry. The client does not implement queue grace.

Focused contention checkpoint:194 native/client/loader tests passed, zero failures/skips, `verification/catalog-busy-focused.txt`. Deterministic cases cover odd and torn reads, recovery, malformed payloads, header/session invalidation even during busy reads, unavailable growth, getter immutability, and no command/proof reuse while busy. The earlier2139-test aggregate predates this narrowly scoped client-status change; the parent owns the final aggregate after its queue grace change.

A follow-up contention regression covers publication beginning after the reader observes an even sequence but before it validates offer count, catalog count/stage, kind/why, internal-name length, UTF8 length or UTF8 bytes. Partial fields under a changed sequence now retry, then report busy if no coherent attempt succeeds. Stable malformed data remains immediately invalid; header/session corruption still overrides busy. The new fixtures also prove same-call recovery after a completed publication and refusal of cached offers during/after sequence changes. Final author focused checkpoint:204 tests passed, `verification/catalog-torn-validation-focused.txt`. The parent owns the subsequent aggregate.

# Mandatory selected-destination dispatch proof, mailbox v3

## Change and scope

Only `hosted-city-v034-candidate` changes. The frozen nearby/travel v0.33 folders are not modified. This fixes a dispatch race: a page could enqueue an eligible host JOIN while inside its selected trigger, move outside that trigger before the native pump, yet remain near the host. The old host/lobby/event-only native check could still dispatch.

Every v3 JOIN now requires BOTH the original exact fresh native host/lobby/event offer and the exact selected destination/context. There is no legacy one-argument or unguarded fallback. This is not travel, hosting, race creation, a generic Enter action, or a permission to join from catalog data alone.

## Client contract

`join(offer, expectedDestination, expectedContext)`:

1. Retain the existing offer WeakMap proof, exact snapshot sequence/time/session/epoch, active native state, pending ACK and eligible-world guards.
2. Obtain another coherent native snapshot. Require a valid catalog, a unique matching destination and exact caller context `{stage, carId, raceTableId, triggerFirst, triggerEnd}`.
3. Compare intended destination fields: event/trigger/marker identity, first track/type/reverse/laps/stage, category, SUV requirement, heat count/all heat tuples, native kind/why, route XYZ, visual XYZ, box, heading and trigger size. Display names and caller race index are not authority.
4. Require this snapshot's actual native current spot to match the destination trigger/marker/kind and complete offered race descriptor.
5. Serialize only the fresh decoded native row and context into the command. Never serialize caller-supplied pointer values or geometry as authority. Missing or changed intent/context refuses without writing.

The parent queue passes its stored selected context after its current-selection checks. The client does not infer a missing selection. Snapshot contention still returns busy with no cached JOIN permission.

## Mailbox and proof layout

Version3, size54736, unchanged registration kind/magic. Existing status/offer/catalog offsets remain unchanged. Catalog publication ends at54560. The separate command proof occupies54560..54735,176 bytes. Profile and client require `destinationProof={version:1, offset:54560, size:176}`.

The command seqlock at64 brackets all old command fields and the complete proof. Native snapshot publication clears only the status/catalog range, never the command proof. Stop, Arm and Heartbeat zero the proof under the command seqlock. Existing reserved Stop capacity and final dispatch CAS remain intact.

Proof offsets relative to54560:

|Offset|Data|
|---|---|
|0|Proof schema version1|
|4|Fresh source snapshot even sequence|
|8|Activation epoch|
|12|Current catalog/career stage|
|16/20/24/28|Car ID, race-table ID, trigger-span first/end|
|32..151|First120 bytes of the fresh numeric catalog row: all identity/category/kind/why/race-index, signed GPSXYZ, visualXYZ, box, second/third heat tuples|
|152/156|HeadingXY f32 bit representations|
|160|Trigger record size|
|164|Native session ID|
|168/172|Required zero reserved words|

Numeric float comparisons at dispatch are exact native bit comparisons. GPS coordinates retain signed32 bit representations. Names, localized labels and their lengths are excluded entirely. Unused heat tuples must be zero.

## Final native boundary

After the unchanged unique fresh native offer search, but before final dispatch CAS:

- `destinationMatches` checks proof version, source snapshot sequence, epoch/session and reserved words.
- It calls the authored full catalog validator, checking all required native tables, committed pages, source stage/span, trigger-chain membership, race membership, geometry, categories/heats and native reasons again.
- It compares current native career stage, actual player-car pointer, race-table base and trigger span to the proof.
- It calls exact native `mp_spot_here` and validates that returned pointer belongs to the current published native spot array. This rechecks actual car containment and native overlap selection at execution time.
- The selected spot's native race pointer must equal the freshly offered native race pointer. Every numeric proof field is compared to these validated native sources, including full geometry and all heats.
- Only then may the existing command sequence/epoch/request/op CAS claim dispatch and invoke the retained native JOIN path.

Command pointer-like values are only compared as opaque IDs. They are never dereferenced. Stop before CAS still cancels; Stop after committed CAS cannot unsend a native request. No synchronous native mutation lies between the destination comparison and the claim.

## Verification

`verification/destination-proof-focused.txt`:308 native/client/loader tests pass, zero failures/skips. Includes current composed v0.33 original-body/section preservation and original-module compile, matching profile rebuild and failure/unknown-build fallback.

New cases include:

- Passive movement after enqueue outside selected box but still within host proximity: zero sends, idle state, consumed refusal.
- Trigger disappearance/replacement/changed native overlap choice; same-hash race-pointer replacement; car/table/span/stage changes.
- Coherent box changes, all route/visual/heading coordinates, trigger size, type/track/reverse/laps/stage, category/SUV/kind/why and all URL heat tuples changing after enqueue.
- Every one of44 command proof words independently mutated; missing proof; forged unreadable trigger ID. All refuse without dereferencing caller IDs.
- Labels/internal names changing does not alter destination authority. Command proof survives native snapshot publication.
- Stop clears all proof words and cancels unclaimed JOIN; retained before/after-CAS interleaving tests still pass.
- Missing/wrong client proof capability, absent caller intent/context, changed intended descriptor/context and mismatched current spot all refuse. Client serialization uses the fresh native row, not caller display fields/race index.

Reviewer script `review/city-catalog-dispatch-repro.cjs` now prints `nativeSends:0`, `nativeState:0` and null current spot after moving to x10 outside selected[-5,5]. Its old assertion expecting2 sends intentionally fails; observed output is saved in `verification/destination-proof-review-repro.txt` for the reviewer to update independently.

No live original-game instance, browser, network, installation, travel or release action was performed. The parent owns final aggregate and independent approval after this checkpoint.

# Independent city catalog and v0.33 composition review

Reviewed 2026-11-10 UTC. Scope: `hosted-city-v034-candidate`, composed onto frozen `combined-v033-integration`, with city catalog/selector and nearby-hosted queue. Re-reviewed after mandatory mailbox-v3 destination binding. No travel implementation is present or approved.

## Verdict

**Approved within the reviewed offline catalog/client/native/queue/composition scope. No unresolved blocking finding remains.** The original exact-destination dispatch race is independently reproduced as fixed by mandatory mailbox-v3 destination proof. The read-only catalog, versioned decoder, bounded busy-grace paths, cancellation behavior, and v0.33 preservation pass this review. This is not live multiplayer approval, travel approval, or a final full-aggregate claim; the coordinator will rerun the aggregate against this checkpoint.

Production sources and the frozen baseline were not edited. Only files under `review/` were written.

## Resolved finding: selected-trigger validity between enqueue and native dispatch

**Previously blocking in mailbox v2; fixed in the reviewed mailbox v3.** The old unconsumed catalog JOIN could dispatch after the player left the selected trigger, provided the same host remained within its broader native nearby radius. The following describes the original defect, not the final source:

- `extension/hosted-session.js:115-123` checks the catalog selection against the current spot's trigger ID, marker hash, kind and event descriptor. This is a page-side snapshot check.
- `extension/hosted-session.js:222-232` passes only the original fresh offer to the client.
- `extension/hosted-native.js:146-155` proves that offer against the latest coherent snapshot, but `command()` at lines 115-120 transmits only host, lobby and event hash alongside command/time/epoch fields. It carries no chosen-trigger or catalog-context proof.
- `tools/hosted-core.cjs:143-160` independently revalidates the native UI/session gates and nearby host/lobby/event hash, then uses the existing final command CAS. It does not revalidate the selected trigger, catalog row, car/source context, or geometry before dispatch.
- Native `mp_here` checks lobby eligibility and a 15m radius, not membership in the selected trigger. Native JOIN itself also does not restore the missing destination check.

### Original independent reproduction

The original repro used the real Queue and mailbox client plus the existing bounded synthetic native fixture. It never instantiated the original game module or contacted a server. `review/city-catalog-dispatch-repro.cjs` now retains that exact scenario with corrected zero-send regression assertions.

1. Publish and select one valid catalog destination with trigger box `[-5,-5,5,5]`, with the car at x=0 and an eligible native host at x=0.
2. Arm, acknowledge, then enqueue the queue's exact original offered JOIN. No send has happened yet.
3. Before the next native pump/dispatch claim, move the synthetic car passively to x=10. The car is outside the selected trigger but still 10m from the host.
4. Run the native pump.

Observed output:

```json
{"selectedBox":[-5,-5,5,5],"carX":10,"afterDispatchSpot":null,"requestWasPending":true,"nativeSends":2,"nativeState":2,"currentHost":102,"currentLobby":202}
```

The old native operation sent the host/hub JOIN even though there was no selected native spot at dispatch. A subsequent page poll or Stop could not unsend it. This was a different issue from the previously fixed Stop/claim race.

### Resolution and independent verification

Mailbox v3 has a 54,736-byte allocation and a mandatory, separate 176-byte destination-proof region at offset 54,560. Version/schema mismatch and legacy one-argument JOIN fail closed. The proof is written/cleared under the existing command seqlock and is outside the native catalog clear/publication range.

The reviewed flow now requires:

1. Queue selection has complete validated car/race-table/trigger-span context. It passes the original fresh offered object, the exact selected descriptor, and the stored selection context.
2. Client verifies the original offer proof and unique fresh offered identity, then matches selected numeric destination/context to a fresh native catalog row and current native spot. Only that fresh row is serialized. Caller names and caller race-index substitutions are not trusted.
3. Native `$join` resolves the unique currently eligible nearby offer, then calls `$destinationMatches`, then performs the original final command CAS, then invokes native JOIN. There is no proofless fallback.
4. `$destinationMatches` revalidates the complete current catalog, stage/car/table/span/session/epoch, exact native `mp_spot_here` result and its published-row membership, exact native offered-race pointer, event/marker/type/category/SUV/kind/why/heat data, route/visual/box/heading geometry and trigger size. Command-supplied IDs are compared only; none are dereferenced.
5. Stop supersession during validation changes the command sequence, so the final CAS cannot claim the old request. A Stop after that CAS cannot unsend the already committed JOIN and disarms on the next pump, preserving the documented boundary.

Running `node review/city-catalog-dispatch-repro.cjs` now succeeds with:

```json
{"selectedBox":[-5,-5,5,5],"carX":10,"afterDispatchSpot":null,"requestWasPending":true,"nativeSends":0,"nativeState":0,"currentHost":0,"currentLobby":0}
```

Log: `review/city-catalog-dispatch-v3-verification.txt`.

The independent focused rerun also covers after-enqueue trigger/source/car/stage/event/geometry mutations, all URL heat tuples, every one of the 44 proof words, missing/forged proof, exact native offered-race pointer, proof persistence across catalog publication, Stop proof clearing, Stop before/after CAS, unchanged valid exact joins and full Queue/client/native trip/return/retry integration. Display-label changes remain non-authoritative.

## Verified positive results

### Catalog/native reader

- The catalog reads the published `g_spot.s` array, never `nw`, with capacity 160 and fixed 336-byte output rows within the original 54,560-byte snapshot area of the 54,736-byte owned allocation.
- Its authored fragment calls only authored read/validation helpers. No native action/formatter/GPS/lobby function is introduced by catalog enumeration.
- Required ranges, every covered guest page, race table membership, variable-size trigger boundaries, stage/span consistency, completed-sweep stamp, geometry, kind/why, heat tuples and duplicate trigger identities are checked before publication.
- Distinct native triggers with the same marker remain distinct destinations. Selector ambiguity checks reject conflicting event identities.
- Optional names are bounded and validated; missing/corrupt optional lookup data falls back to empty/numeric display without changing destination identity. UI inserts text through `textContent`.
- Catalog metadata and rows are frozen, and catalog rows never enter the private offer-proof WeakMap. Selection and pure observation do not create offers or send actions.
- Availability/restriction text does not promise career credit. No raw locked/future career race-table expansion or travel is present.

### Seqlock and bounded contention grace

- The mailbox v3 profile/size/catalog/destination-proof schema must match before decode. One snapshot sequence covers offers and catalog.
- `snapshotStatus` distinguishes ready, busy, invalid and unavailable. Malformed fields reread the sequence before being classified invalid; changed/odd publications are discarded and retried, with no cached snapshot returned.
- Exhausted odd/torn attempts recheck header/session so invalid attachments cannot masquerade as contention.
- Busy arm/heartbeat/JOIN reads do not issue those commands, and old offers do not survive a sequence change.
- Queue grace is allowed only for explicit busy, within 250ms of the last coherent native-time observation. It returns before queue heartbeat/JOIN, disables selected-offer resolution and race ownership, and does not extend itself through repeated busy reads.
- Start and selection cannot use busy observations. Unknown/invalid/unavailable status, malformed samples and exceptions do not receive grace. Manual stop/permission withdrawal remains immediate. Grace expiry stops the session and requires explicit Start.

# Hosted bridge: offline integration evidence

## Scope

This candidate composes a default-off native hosted-lobby bridge inside the existing verified-original `ai.js` compile pipeline. It supports only original SHA-256 `128e2b5816a8eace4b768aec920318a1613da8235801a361e2009e96550be1d6` (93af6ccb). Other supported AI profiles retain v0.32 behavior and receive no hosted capability.

No original game instance was created, no game server was contacted, no live lobby was joined, and no worker source was injected. Full original/combined modules are compiled only. Executed fixtures are synthetic, network-free modules containing explicitly selected native function bodies and controlled stubs.

## Integration and preservation

- `tools/hosted-build.cjs` generates `extension/hosted-profile.js` from authored WAT. The shipped profile contains authored function bodies only, no extracted original function bodies.
- The sole change to an existing v0.32 body is caller f22659, at its pinned original offset81052. Its original padded call to f22706 is redirected to an appended wrapper.
- The wrapper invokes original f22706 exactly once, first, with all seven original arguments unchanged. It then invokes the hosted pump using actual native host time/in-roam/world-running arguments.
- Original f22706, all original function indexes, original types/global prefixes, tables, data, exports, drivers and results remain unchanged. New functions/types/private globals are appended. No game-native callable is exported to page JavaScript.
- Independent runtime compilation tests compare every original v0.32 body except the caller, all unchanged section payloads, and original type/function prefixes. The checked-in authored profile must equal a fresh build exactly.
- A hosted transform or compile error falls back to already verified v0.32-patched bytes, not the unpatched game. Original module profile and capabilities are retained; only the separate `AI.getHostedProfile(module)` is absent. Native tuner preparation receives the untouched original module bytes.

## Ownership and protocol

The main-thread pump allocates768 bytes once via exact native calloc f23963. The returned aligned physical range must be host memory and within current memory bounds. Allocation/registration failures latch disabled, without retry every frame. The allocation is never freed while the page might retain it. Native f4 (`nfsu2.register`) publishes extension-only kind0x4e465348; normal game kinds1..7 are untouched. The page must bind registrations to its verified active worker/module/memory session.

Private appended globals own mailbox pointer, initialization, accepted epoch, active status, consumed request/command sequences, snapshot sequence, native clock history, heartbeat, acknowledgement and result. The page cannot supply native frame flags, current time, scratch pointers or native callees.

Mailbox version1:

- 0 magic0x484f5354;4 version;8 size768;12 instance session marker.
- 16 native snapshot seqlock;20 accepted epoch;24 native MP state;28 inRoam;32 worldRuns;36 current eligibility;40 native time i64.
- 48 acknowledged request sequence;52 signed result;56 current lobby;60 current host.
- 64 command seqlock;68 requested epoch;72 operation0Stop/1Arm/2Tick/3Join;76 monotonic request;80 echoed native time i64;88 host;92 lobby;96 event hash.
- 104 native activation status.
- 128 reader payload: count;132 spot-present;136 spot kind;160 spot row;192 offers, at most16 rows of32 bytes. Row fields are host,lobby,eventHash,track,rawType,reverse,laps,stage.

The registration session marker is constant1 within the native instance; identity is additionally bounded by verified worker/module/memory and unique owned pointer. A replacement module/worker must detach the old client, rather than treating the marker as globally unique. Duplicate different registrations fail closed. The client handles page-observed memory growth without retaining detached views.

ARM requires a new higher epoch, fresh native heartbeat and current eligible idle state. TICK maintains observation during native joining/lobby/countdown/trip/loading/results/return, without authorizing a join. JOIN is consumed exactly once and must match a unique fresh native allowed host/lobby/race identity at execution time. There is no create, alternate-host, far-join or navigation fallback.

A heartbeat expires after500000 native microseconds. Native clock rollback invalidates activation. Unknown/old/replayed/wrapped sequences are refused. Stop clears the page's unconsumed payload, raises the epoch and prevents automatic re-arm. Finishing or losing a native lobby is not proof of a race win.

### Stop linearization

After native current-UI/eligibility checks and fresh enumeration, a final compare-exchange claims commandSeq from expected even value to value+2 immediately before original mp_join. A Stop that acquires or replaces the mailbox command before this claim prevents dispatch. Once the claim succeeds, dispatch is committed: Stop cannot unsend that JOIN, revoke host acceptance or leave an already entered lobby. If the native claim wins between the client’s sequence read and its Stop write-lock, the client retries Stop once only when the observed sequence advanced by exactly two with the same JOIN operation, request and epoch. A subsequent pump then consumes the published Stop and disables further commands. Unrelated contention still fails closed; heartbeat expiry disables activation if no Stop can be published. Sequence headroom is reserved, with no wrap.

## Native gates

The original reviewed reader/join preflight is preserved: physical memory/stack bounds, directly consumed guest pointers and bitmap pages, finite coordinates, ordered spot/event boxes, bounded counts, native race-table membership, HUD timestamp and advert freshness, native career/car ownership, exact unique tuple, and fresh mp_here eligibility. The existing research fixture's100 tests remain unchanged and passing.

Additional exact-current UI gates derive the current player's HUD package and call native f22702 (coop-aware hud_on_top). Native f21210 searches active FE packages and blocks `UI_EngageRaceDialog.fng` at the verified immutable native string pointer. Generic dialog `[0x838974]` remains an independent gate. The authored UI preflight bounds the actual current player/HUD, FE manager and both FE lists, co-op player/HUD and strings before these native calls. Missing/invalid/cyclic/unterminated graphs reject.

Native states are0IDLE,1HOST,2ASKED,3IN,4COUNT,5TRIP. Result1 means only that original mp_join issued its normal request. Result2 acknowledges ARM/TICK. No host acceptance, race start, completion or reward is fabricated.

Run within this candidate:

    node tools/hosted-build.cjs
    node --test tests/hosted-native.test.cjs tests/hosted-client.test.cjs tests/hosted-loader.test.cjs

Fixture limitations: original mp_frame is an argument/order recorder; allocator implementation f23959 and registration are controlled stubs (exact native calloc itself executes); platform sends are intercepted; career ownership/rating caches/lock/log helpers are controlled. UI fixtures execute all nine exact native UI bodies, including FE traversal/indirect callback/table slot20562 and libc helpers, with no UI-native stubs. The preflight covers identified directly consumed structures, not arbitrary corrupted/concurrently mutated native memory or every transitive game invariant. Native runtime invariants and the verified game-thread hook remain necessary.     async find({goal,onProgress}){dynoLog.finds++;this.busy=true;onProgress({evaluations:2,budget:120});return new Promise((resolve,reject)=>{this.fail=reject;this.finish=()=>{this.fail=null;this.busy=false;this.outcome={goal,improved:true,baselineResult:{peakPowerKw:200,peakTorqueNm:300},bestResult:{peakPowerKw:220,peakTorqueNm:310},evaluations:40};resolve(this.outcome);};});}

test('actual page keeps switches through pause/loading/new car and safely reapplies',async()=>{
  const f=await pageFixture();f.change('boost',true);f.change('grip',true);f.change('nos',true);f.run(3);
  assert.equal(f.read(0x2dc),0.75);assert.equal(f.d.getFloat32(f.wheels[0]+0x188,true),Math.fround(1.3));
  f.put(f.race,6);f.drive(0);f.run();assert.equal(f.read(0x2dc),0.5);assert.equal(f.prefs().boost,true);assert.equal(f.prefs().grip,true);
  f.put(A.FLOW,4);f.run();assert.equal(f.prefs().nos,true);
  const newCar=0xe30000,newRide=0xe32000;
  new Uint8Array(f.memory.buffer).copyWithin(newCar,f.car,f.car+0x9e4);
  new Uint8Array(f.memory.buffer).copyWithin(newRide,f.ride,f.ride+0x584);
  f.put(newCar+0x10,newRide);f.put(f.player+4,newCar);f.put(A.FLOW,6);f.put(f.race,4);f.drive(2);
  f.run(2);assert.equal(f.d.getFloat32(newRide+0x10+0x2dc,true),0.5);
  f.run();assert.equal(f.d.getFloat32(newRide+0x10+0x2dc,true),0.75);assert.equal(f.read(0x2dc),0.5);
});

  assert.equal(f.aiLog.updates.at(-1).safe,false);assert.equal(f.read(0x2dc),0.5);assert.equal(f.d.getUint32(f.car+A.NOS_LEFT,true),0);
  f.press('F8');assert.equal(f.nodes['tools-panel'].hidden,false);f.change('online',true);f.run(3);
  assert.equal(f.aiLog.updates.at(-1).safe,true);assert.equal(f.aiLog.updates.at(-1).allowNetwork,true);assert.equal(f.read(0x2dc),0.75);assert.equal(f.read(0x2c0),0);assert.equal(f.d.getUint32(f.car+A.NOS_LEFT,true),40000);assert.equal(f.d.getFloat32(f.wheels[0]+0x188,true),Math.fround(1.3));assert.match(f.nodes.live.textContent,/Online\/LAN opt-in/);assert.match(f.nodes.enabled.textContent,/selected/);
  const stops=f.aiLog.stops;f.change('online',false);assert.ok(f.aiLog.stops>stops);assert.equal(f.read(0x2dc),0.5);assert.equal(f.read(0x2c0),150);assert.equal(f.d.getFloat32(f.wheels[0]+0x188,true),1);
  f.put(f.car+A.NOS_LEFT,123);f.run(4);assert.equal(f.d.getUint32(f.car+A.NOS_LEFT,true),123);assert.equal(f.aiLog.updates.at(-1).safe,false);assert.equal(f.prefs().boost,true);assert.equal(f.nodes['tools-panel'].hidden,false);
  f.change('online',true);f.run(3);assert.equal(f.read(0x2dc),0.75);f.focus(false);f.run();assert.equal(f.read(0x2dc),0.5);assert.equal(f.aiLog.updates.at(-1).safe,false);
  f.focus(true);f.run(3);assert.equal(f.read(0x2dc),0.75);f.press('F7');f.run();assert.equal(f.prefs().ai,false);assert.equal(f.prefs().online,true);
  f.press('F9');f.run();assert.equal(f.prefs().online,false);assert.equal(f.nodes.online.checked,false);assert.equal(f.prefs().boost,false);assert.equal(f.read(0x2dc),0.5);assert.equal(f.aiLog.updates.at(-1).allowNetwork,false);
});

  f.put(A.DRAG,drag?1:0);f.drive(drag?1:2);f.run();const last=f.aiLog.updates.at(-1);

 }
});

  assert.deepEqual(f.aiLog.keys,[]);assert.match(f.nodes['drag-ai-state'].textContent,/waits for GO/);

  f.put(f.race,4);f.run();assert.deepEqual(f.aiLog.keys,[]);

 }
});

test('a different unverified module cannot inherit trust by reusing verified memory',async()=>{
 let lookups=0;const f=await pageFixture(null,true,true,{verifier:()=>++lookups===1?{revision:'6f4f1e4e',capabilities:{legacy:true,ai:true,pace:true,corner:true,walls:true,dyno:true,dragAI:true}}:null});
 const replacement=new WebAssembly.Module(Uint8Array.from([0,97,115,109,1,0,0,0]));f.worker.postMessage({mod:replacement,memory:f.memory,slot:0});f.worker.emit({t:'register',kind:5,ptr:f.status});
 assert.equal(lookups,2);f.change('boost',true);f.change('grip',true);f.change('nos',true);const before=Buffer.from(f.memory.buffer);f.run(5);assert.deepEqual(Buffer.from(f.memory.buffer),before);assert.equal(f.read(0x2dc),0.5);assert.match(f.nodes.live.textContent,/not verified/);
});

 f.change('boost',true);f.change('grip',true);f.run(3);assert.equal(f.read(0x2dc),0.75);assert.ok(f.d.getFloat32(f.wheels[0]+0x188,true)>1);
 f.worker.postMessage({mod:new WebAssembly.Module(Uint8Array.from([0,97,115,109,1,0,0,0])),memory:f.memory,slot:0});assert.equal(f.read(0x2dc),0.5);assert.equal(f.d.getFloat32(f.wheels[0]+0x188,true),1);const before=Buffer.from(f.memory.buffer);f.run(5);assert.deepEqual(Buffer.from(f.memory.buffer),before);
});

test('combined power and grip stress does not compound through 5000 adjustments and exact restores',()=>{
 const f=performanceFixture(),physics=0xe18000,wheels=[0xe19000,0xe1a000,0xe1b000,0xe1c000];f.put(f.car+0x34,physics);
 wheels.forEach((w,i)=>{f.put(physics+0x38+i*4,w);f.d.setFloat32(w+0x188,1,true);});
 const base=f.read(0x230);
 for(let i=0;i<5000;i++){
  const s=f.e.state(),power=1+(i%21)/10,grip=1+(i%11)/10;
  f.e.tunePerformance(s,power,i%2===0);f.e.tuneGrip(s,grip);
  assert.equal(f.read(0x230),Math.fround(base*power));assert.equal(f.read(0x2dc),Math.fround(.5*power));assert.equal(f.read(0x2c0),i%2===0?0:150);
  wheels.forEach(w=>assert.equal(f.d.getFloat32(w+0x188,true),Math.fround(grip)));
  if(i%7===0){f.e.restorePerformance(s);f.e.restoreGrip(s);assert.equal(f.read(0x230),base);assert.equal(f.read(0x2dc),.5);wheels.forEach(w=>assert.equal(f.d.getFloat32(w+0x188,true),1));}
 }
 f.e.restorePerformance(f.e.state());f.e.restoreGrip(f.e.state());assert.equal(f.read(0x230),base);assert.equal(f.read(0x2c0),150);
});
test('page power/grip survive 100 pause/resume cycles without carrying multipliers into baseline',async()=>{
 const f=await pageFixture(null,true);f.change('boost',true);f.input('power',3);f.change('grip',true);f.input('grip-factor',2);
 for(let i=0;i<100;i++){
  f.run(3);assert.equal(f.read(0x2dc),1.5);f.wheels.forEach(w=>assert.equal(f.d.getFloat32(w+0x188,true),2));
  f.focus(false);f.run();assert.equal(f.read(0x2dc),.5);f.wheels.forEach(w=>assert.equal(f.d.getFloat32(w+0x188,true),1));
  f.focus(true);
 }
 f.press('F9');assert.equal(f.read(0x2dc),.5);f.wheels.forEach(w=>assert.equal(f.d.getFloat32(w+0x188,true),1));
});

function interleaveBeforeCompare(e,action){const real=e.compareFloat.bind(e);let ran=false;e.compareFloat=(...args)=>{if(!ran){ran=true;action();}return real(...args);};return ()=>ran;}
test('apply and restore refuse a retired grip/ride identity immediately before a field operation',()=>{
 for(const type of ['power','grip'])for(const restoring of [false,true]){
  const f=type==='power'?performanceFixture():gripFixture(),s=f.e.state();
  const apply=()=>type==='power'?f.e.tunePerformance(s,1.5,true):f.e.tuneGrip(s,1.3);
  const restore=()=>type==='power'?f.e.restorePerformance(s):f.e.restoreGrip(s);
  if(restoring)apply();
  const retired=type==='power'?[...Array.from({length:9},(_,i)=>f.pi+0x230+i*4),f.pi+0x2dc,f.pi+0x2c0]:f.wheels.map(w=>w+0x188);
  const ran=interleaveBeforeCompare(f.e,()=>{f.put(f.car+(type==='power'?0x10:0x34),0xe80000);retired.forEach(p=>f.d.setFloat32(p,99,true));});
  restoring?restore():apply();assert(ran(),'interleaving was executed');retired.forEach(p=>assert.equal(f.d.getFloat32(p,true),99));
 }
});
test('compare-and-swap preserves another writer after the final ownership check',()=>{
 for(const restoring of [false,true]){
  const f=gripFixture(),s=f.e.state();if(restoring)f.e.tuneGrip(s,1.3);
  const real=f.e.compareFloat.bind(f.e);let ran=false;
  f.e.compareFloat=(p,expected,value,guard)=>real(p,expected,value,()=>{const result=guard();if(!ran){ran=true;f.d.setFloat32(p,.8,true);}return result;});
  restoring?f.e.restoreGrip(s):f.e.tuneGrip(s,1.3);assert(ran);assert.equal(f.read()[0],Math.fround(.8));assert.deepEqual(f.read().slice(1),[1,1,1]);
 }
});
test('partial adjustment rolls back only successful owned fields when another field changes',()=>{
 const f=performanceFixture(),s=f.e.state(),real=f.e.compareFloat.bind(f.e);let count=0,ran=false;
 f.e.compareFloat=(p,expected,value,guard)=>{if(++count===4){ran=true;f.d.setFloat32(p,.77,true);}return real(p,expected,value,guard);};
 assert.equal(f.e.tunePerformance(s,2,true).changed,true);assert(ran);assert.equal(f.read(0x230),Math.fround(.2));assert.equal(f.read(0x23c),Math.fround(.77));assert.equal(f.read(0x2dc),.5);assert.equal(f.e.performancePatch,null);
});

  const before=Buffer.from(f.memory.buffer);const result=type==='power'?f.e.tunePerformance(s,1.5,true):type==='grip'?f.e.tuneGrip(s,1.3):f.e.refill(s);

 }

test('unchanged power and grip factors avoid repeat atomic stores',()=>{
 const f=performanceFixture(),g=gripFixture(),s=f.e.state(),t=g.e.state();f.e.tunePerformance(s,2,true);g.e.tuneGrip(t,1.5);
 const original=Atomics.compareExchange;let count=0;Atomics.compareExchange=(...args)=>{count++;return original(...args);};
 try{for(let i=0;i<50;i++){f.e.tunePerformance(s,2,true);g.e.tuneGrip(t,1.5);}}finally{Atomics.compareExchange=original;}
 assert.equal(count,0);
});

 const profile=require('../extension/next-profile.js'),f=await pageFixture(null,true,false,{revision:profile.revision,profile});f.drive(1);f.put(0x89e7b0,1);f.put(0x89e7e3,1);f.change('ai',true);f.change('race-pace',true);f.input('race-pace-factor',1.35);f.change('race-corner-assist',true);f.input('race-corner-factor',.85);f.input('race-corner-margin',20);f.input('race-braking',.7);f.change('walls',true);f.change('cars',true);f.run();
 const fields=x=>[x.raceCornerAssist,x.raceCornerFactor,x.raceCornerMargin,x.raceBraking,x.pace];const solo=fields(f.aiLog.updates.at(-1));assert.equal(solo[0],true);
 for(const [address,value] of [[A.MODE,8],[A.MODE,512],[0x866a14,1],[0x8669f4,1],[0x89cf69,1]]){
  f.put(address,value);f.run();assert.equal(f.aiLog.updates.at(-1).raceCornerAssist,false);assert.match(f.nodes['race-corner-state'].textContent,/Paused online/);
  f.change('online',true);f.run();assert.deepEqual(fields(f.aiLog.updates.at(-1)),solo);assert.equal(f.aiLog.updates.at(-1).safe,true);assert.equal(f.aiLog.updates.at(-1).state.network,true);assert.match(f.nodes['walls-state'].textContent,/Paused online/);assert.match(f.nodes['cars-state'].textContent,/Paused online/);assert.equal(f.d.getUint32(address,true),value);
  f.change('online',false);f.run();assert.equal(f.aiLog.updates.at(-1).raceCornerAssist,false);assert.equal(f.aiLog.updates.at(-1).safe,false);f.put(address,0);
 }
 assert.equal(f.d.getUint32(0x89e7e3,true),1);f.put(A.MODE,8);f.change('online',true);f.run();f.press('F9');f.run();assert.equal(f.aiLog.updates.at(-1).raceCornerAssist,false);assert.equal(f.aiLog.updates.at(-1).allowNetwork,false);assert.equal(f.nodes['race-corner-assist'].checked,false);

});

// Named tool profiles use the real page and the same guarded game-memory harness.
const Profiles=require('../extension/tool-profiles.js');
const profileRecord=f=>JSON.parse(f.profileStorage.get(Profiles.KEY));
function saveToolProfile(f,name='My driving',consent=false){f.input('profile-name',name);f.change('profile-network',consent);f.click('profile-save');return profileRecord(f).profiles.at(-1);}
function chooseToolProfile(f,profile){f.change('profile-select',profile.id);}
const fullProfileCaps={legacy:true,ai:true,pace:true,corner:true,walls:true,cars:true,dyno:true,dragAI:true,onlineTraffic:true,onlinePlayers:true,nativeDragOverheat:true};

test('named tool profiles survive a browser restart but never autoload by default',async()=>{
 const first=await pageFixture(null,true,true,{capabilities:fullProfileCaps});
 for(const id of ['ai','nos','drag','drag-no-blowout','boost','grip','walls','cars','traffic','players','online','tester','dyno-enable'])first.change(id,true);
 first.input('power','2.1');first.input('rpm','7400');first.change('dyno-goal','peakTorque');
 const p=saveToolProfile(first,'Everything');assert.equal(p.settings.dynoEnabled,true);assert.equal(p.settings.dynoGoal,'peakTorque');assert.equal(p.settings.dragNoBlowout,true);assert.equal(p.networkConsent,false);assert.equal(profileRecord(first).auto,null);
 const restarted=await pageFixture(null,true,true,{profileStorage:first.profileStorage,capabilities:fullProfileCaps});
 for(const id of ['ai','nos','drag','boost','grip','walls','cars','online','dyno-enable'])assert.equal(restarted.nodes[id].checked,false,id);
 chooseToolProfile(restarted,p);restarted.click('profile-load');
 for(const id of ['ai','nos','drag','drag-no-blowout','boost','grip','walls','cars','tester','dyno-enable'])assert.equal(restarted.nodes[id].checked,true,id);
 for(const id of ['online','traffic','players'])assert.equal(restarted.nodes[id].checked,false,id);
 assert.equal(restarted.nodes.power.value,2.1);assert.equal(restarted.nodes.rpm.value,7400);assert.equal(restarted.nodes['dyno-goal'].value,'peakTorque');
 assert.equal(restarted.dynoLog.finds,0);assert.equal(restarted.dynoLog.applies,0);assert.equal(restarted.dynoLog.restores,0);
 assert.doesNotMatch(JSON.stringify(p),/"car"|baseline|draft|applied|diagnostic|memory|pointer/);
});
test('manual profile loading never borrows network permission from current controls or unsaved checkbox',async()=>{
 const f=await pageFixture(null,true,false,{capabilities:fullProfileCaps});
 for(const id of ['online','traffic','players','ai'])f.change(id,true);
 const p=saveToolProfile(f,'No saved consent');f.change('profile-network',true);f.click('profile-load');
 for(const id of ['online','traffic','players'])assert.equal(f.nodes[id].checked,false,id);
 assert.equal(f.nodes.ai.checked,true);assert.equal(profileRecord(f).profiles[0].networkConsent,false);
 for(const id of ['online','traffic','players'])f.change(id,true);
 f.change('profile-network',true);f.click('profile-update');
 f.press('F9');f.click('profile-load');for(const id of ['online','traffic','players'])assert.equal(f.nodes[id].checked,true,id);
 assert.equal(profileRecord(f).profiles[0].id,p.id);
});

 const p=saveToolProfile(f,'Resume me',true);f.change('profile-auto',true);const oldRecord=f.profileStorage.get(Profiles.KEY);

 chooseToolProfile(r,p);r.click('profile-load');assert.equal(r.nodes.ai.checked,true);assert.equal(r.nodes['profile-auto'].checked,false);

 r.change('profile-auto',true);const resumed=await pageFixture(null,true,false,{profileStorage:f.profileStorage});assert.equal(resumed.nodes.ai.checked,true);
});

test('profile load refuses pending drift and cancels busy tuner without restoring or staging any game preset',async()=>{
 const f=await pageFixture(null,true,true);f.change('nos',true);saveToolProfile(f,'Saved');f.change('nos',false);
 // Set up a genuine asynchronous native drift request in the input ring.
 const ptr=0xf10000;f.put(ptr,0x4e494e50);f.put(ptr+4,2);f.put(ptr+3*4,1024);f.put(ptr+7*4,1);f.worker.emit({t:'register',kind:3,ptr});
 f.change('drift',true);assert.equal(f.d.getUint32(ptr+4*4,true),1);f.click('profile-load');assert.equal(f.nodes.nos.checked,false);assert.match(f.nodes['profile-state'].textContent,/drift request/);assert.equal(f.d.getUint32(ptr+4*4,true),1);
 f.run(61);f.click('profile-load');assert.equal(f.nodes.nos.checked,true);
 f.change('nos',false);f.change('dyno-enable',true);f.nodes['dyno-goal'].value='peakPower';f.click('dyno-find');assert.equal(f.dynoLog.instance.busy,true);
 const cancels=f.dynoLog.cancels;f.click('profile-load');assert.ok(f.dynoLog.cancels>cancels);assert.equal(f.nodes.nos.checked,false);assert.match(f.nodes['profile-state'].textContent,/pending game request/);assert.equal(f.dynoLog.applies,0);assert.equal(f.dynoLog.restores,0);
 await new Promise(r=>setImmediate(r));f.dynoLog.instance.pending=Promise.resolve();f.click('profile-load');assert.equal(f.nodes.nos.checked,false);f.dynoLog.instance.pending=null;f.click('profile-load');assert.equal(f.nodes.nos.checked,true);
});

# Selected free-roam event prototype

Research candidate built from frozen v0.32. Not a v0.33 release. No ZIP made.

The user's screenshot identifies the free-roam multiplayer event-start interface: Drag, Stage 5, Runway 15, with Enter / Open a lobby. This is a selectable event location, not a displayed hosted Join card. Open a lobby can be a separate page beside existing hosted cards; it does not prove no host exists. The prototype lets the user choose an observed event even when no hosted card is displayed and watch the currently displayed nearby card for a matching event. It does not inspect all selected locations remotely; the game’s next-lobby control must be used to display other nearby hosts. It does not press Enter, create or join lobbies, drive, travel or change race results.

- New module: extension/hosted-race-list.js
- Existing files changed: page.js (four additive UI/stop hooks), manifest.json (preview name/description and new script)
- Native code and all original v0.32 features, race-only AI, adaptive pace, Drag and Street X are unchanged.
- 25 focused tests cover selection, appearance/absence of hosts, Runway 15 spot cards, no Join without a host, stop controls, CSS visibility, focus retention and preservation.

The next requirement is an exact native allowed-offer identity reader and join-if-still-matching guard. UI text alone cannot guarantee that an Enter is still joining the intended lobby. The native default can create a new lobby if the offer vanished, so this prototype deliberately has no automatic game input.

Current verification: 1,932/1,932 tests pass, including 25 focused selector tests. Independent review approved observation-only behavior; its wording correction is applied: Open a lobby is only the currently displayed page, and does not prove nobody is hosting. Effective visibility and keyed checkbox/focus retention remain tested.

A read-only inspection of the actual connected PC verified the card DOM: #lobby data-v=spot with Drag / Stage 5 · Runway 15 / Enter / Open a lobby. No next-lobby control/count/host roster was exposed on that shown card at inspection. No input or changes were made. This verifies the target interface, not candidate installation, automatic joining or full live behavior.

# NFSU2 Driving Tools: experimental v0.32.0

Unpacked Chrome / Edge / Brave extension for https://nfsu2.xyz/. See `CHANGELOG.md` for this release's changes and verification limits.

## v0.32.0: Race-only automatic driver

In **AI driver**, enable **Race-only automatic driver** to arm the native driver for races you start or join yourself. It waits for the active race/GO state, includes Street X, Drag and Drift, and requests handback in free roam, outrun, results or other ineligible contexts. It does not find, join, start, replay or vote for events.

The existing **Automatic driver** still includes free roam. Selecting either driver mode turns the other off. The race-only switch is **off by default**, stays armed between races on this page, and resets on page reload or profile Load. It is deliberately not added to saved profiles; existing saved choices and storage remain unchanged.

**F7, F9/Stop, or driving-key takeover during a race disarms race-only AI.** Manual steering in free roam leaves it armed. If driving controls are still physically held when entering a race, acquisition waits until they are released. Turning the switch off requests native handback. A genuine native manual request, finished/totaled state, failed-control latch or watchdog is not forced back to AI.

Online races still need the existing **Allow network tools** permission. Exact build, current ownership, race, focus/menu, native driver and handback guards are retained. A selected switch is not proof of active ownership; the HUD and local log show the effective request and native observations separately.

Optional **Adaptive road-race speed** is also included below. It remains off by default and leaves Street X unchanged. Neither option changes steering, shifting, NOS, game saves or native AI code. Live race efficacy and browser appearance remain unverified.

**Verification:** the complete combined release passes **1,907 automated tests, zero failures/skips/cancellations**, including race-only eligibility/lifecycle, optional adaptive mode, joint Street X/online/stop behavior and all retained features. Independent tests additionally cover production native handback and cached-route reconstruction. All four supported patched game module outputs remain byte-identical to v0.31.

For an existing installation, replace matching files in the already loaded extension folder, click **Reload** on that extension's browser card, then refresh the game. Verify **0.32.0**. Do not remove/re-add the extension or create a different folder just for this update.

## Optional adaptive road-race speed

A new **default-off, session-only** option coordinates the existing native route planner. Its separate straight-target ceiling defaults to **1.30×** and ranges from 1.00× to 2.00×. The native route uses distance to known corners to lower its target in advance while retaining a higher target on sufficiently long straights. This is a planned target factor, not a physical speed cap or a measured speed increase.

Enable either **Race-only automatic driver** or **Automatic driver**, then **Adaptive road-race speed** in AI driver → Road-race settings. Online use also requires **Allow network tools**. Adaptive mode uses the existing Race corner speed, Race sharp-turn margin and Race braking factor values, even when the separate Road-race hairpin assist switch is off. Lower braking factor requests earlier braking. It overrides the effective custom race pace only in eligible ordinary road races, without changing any saved switch or slider.

**Street X keeps the exact existing pace, corner and braking selections.** Adaptive mode is dormant in actual/forced Street X and the known online Street X mode. Drag, Drift/forced variants, Outrun and free roam are also excluded. Selecting adaptive mode does not turn on Automatic driver or network permission.

The optional ceiling stays constant while driving. The existing native route envelope varies by distance; JavaScript does not switch pace or reconstruct the driver at every corner. A deliberate setting or race-mode change may still require the existing OFF/acknowledgement/ON route reconstruction. Manual takeover, race end, permission withdrawal and the existing watchdog remain in force.

F7/manual driving keys stop AI and leave the optional selection dormant. F9/Stop, profile Load and page reload turn adaptive mode off. It is not added to saved tool profiles or legacy session preferences. Blur, hidden page and menus pause it normally. Turn it off to return to the prior controls after native handoff.

The HUD and local log distinguish a request, matching native pace acknowledgement, and observed corner/braking hook evidence. These counters do not measure braking success, safe corner entry or a clean lap. There is no new steering, obstacle avoidance, NOS control, added route horizon, opponent manipulation or collision protection. Higher targets can still cause crashes. Start at 1.30× and assess one change at a time.

Only page orchestration, a pure selector and bounded diagnostics change. Native hooks, the AI controller, engine tuning, NOS clock correction, Drag-retention fix, tuner and saved-profile implementation remain byte-for-byte unchanged from v0.31. Exact-native synthetic tests support the route-speed envelope; live racing, lap times, wins and browser layout remain unverified.

## Retained v0.31.0: Keep owned Drag AI through settings refreshes

A reproduced publication race could let the game's manual-Drag selector run while the extension refreshed the same active settings. The new guard retains an **already-owned, currently permitted native Drag AI lease** through that brief write. It does not acquire new control, force a real manual request back to AI, or change steering, shifting, NOS or damage.

A separate fix ensures a pause/end/OFF command is acknowledged by the native game before a quick restart can overwrite it. This also covers consecutive matches that reuse the same player, car and race objects. It does not clear the game's failed-control latch while AI remains continuously requested.

**F7/manual takeover, F9/OFF, native finish/totaled states, permission withdrawal, identity changes and the 180-native-frame watchdog remain effective.** Do not use this as a no-crash, no-damage or guaranteed-win feature. Online use still requires the existing explicit Allow network tools opt-in.

The fresh user log shows a request for manual Drag before the observed handback, matching the reproduced ordering. It does not record the rejecting guard, so this is not proof of that run's exact cause. The log came from v0.28. Live handoff prevention remains unverified.

Only the Drag input guard changes in the two supported modern native profiles. The HUD, tuner/static-ride fix, NOS clock correction, working Street X behavior, Drift isolation, saved profiles, collision/corner settings and engine-blowout protection remain combined. No unrelated lane candidate or unverified grip/downforce activation is included.

**Verification:** the final combined suite passes 1,873 tests with no failures/skips/cancellations. Browser appearance and live race efficacy remain unverified.

## Retained v0.30.0: Compact driving information HUD

A small, click-through **Info HUD** appears below the upper-right launcher while the tools menu is closed. **F6** toggles it, or open **F8 → Info HUD**. It starts on and remembers only its display choice in this tab, separately from driving-tool profiles. Opening the menu hides the card until you close it. F7 returns control and F9 still stops driving assists; the HUD itself never enables them.

- **Speed:** existing guarded native speed converted to **km/h**. Zero is shown only when sampled as zero. Unknown builds, invalid car data and paused/missing samples show **Unavailable**, never a guessed or multiplied speed. Older supported builds without verified speed telemetry also show Unavailable.
- **Driver:** observed native AI/manual state, pending handoff, or the reason tools are waiting/paused. A selected AI switch is not called active by itself.
- **Pace:** `req` is the current requested AI target factor; `ack` is a matching native acknowledgement, not measured vehicle speed. A newly selected factor does not reuse an old acknowledgement. Selected pace waits for AI; Drag and Drift retain native pace.
- **Power:** `req` is the selected field multiplier; `set` reports guarded power-field application. It is not measured horsepower or a guaranteed speed increase. Paused, rejected and settling states stay distinct from application.

The HUD is read-only and uses existing observations. Stop, manual takeover, blur, hidden tab, game exit, replacement boot and tuner suspension clear old display evidence. No new physics, AI, speed/power formula, native hook, network permission, tuning, game-save or profile-schema change is included. The complete v0.29 tuner/static-ride fix, online NOS correction, Street X, Drift, Drag and online tools remain together.

**Verification:** 1,788 automated tests pass with no failures/skips/cancellations, including 20 focused HUD tests. Browser layout/fullscreen behavior and live game appearance remain unverified. No screenshot is presented as actual gameplay.

## Retained v0.29.0: Accept verified native car records in the tuner

Arbitrary low addresses remain rejected; the existing heap path and all other safety checks remain.

If another check fails, retain its S-code or export the crash log; later layout protections have not been removed.

The power panel also reports whether power fields were applied, are settling, or are blocked by a specific guard. Exported pace acknowledgement is separate from power application. These are observations, **not a measured speed increase**; no speed, power, driver or network setting is changed by this status addition.

The final v0.29 suite passes **1,768 tests, zero failures/skips/cancellations**. ## Retained v0.28.0: Correct the online Unlimited NOS clock

Unlimited NOS now refreshes an already-active NOS timestamp using the same clock the native game selected. The previous version always used the world clock; in an online fixture where the game's real clock was ahead, that made a full kit immediately appear depleted and caused repeated native stop/restart cycles. The corrected code retains the burst in that exact native test.

This is a reproduced timing defect, **not proof of the clock values in your live run or a guarantee that NOS never stops**. Native AI can still cancel NOS for normal driving decisions. This update does not hold Alt, force activation, suppress native stops or change driving, shifting, steering or lane choice. Inactive and sentinel timestamps remain inactive; network permission and current-car/kit checks remain mandatory.

For an online comparison, use the same ordinary driving situation with **Unlimited NOS** and **Allow network tools** enabled. If tapping remains, use **Export crash log** immediately. The new log samples the selected clock, active-since stamp and kit/resource accounting **before refill**; it contains no pointers. The timestamp flag does not prove successful activation, and sampled logs can miss short transitions.

The v0.28 combined suite passed **1,740 tests, zero failures/skips/cancellations**. Saved tool profiles, working Street X behavior, reviewed Drift isolation, Drag protection, online collision/corner settings and the full tuner with snapshot diagnostics remain together. No native game code or profile was changed. v0.28 did not change tuner capture. The v0.29 native-record correction is described above; any remaining rejection still needs its S-code/log. Live NOS behavior and game-save persistence remain unverified.

## Retained v0.27.0: Identify rejected tuner snapshots

This update replaces the generic “Full tuner snapshot layout is unsupported” message with a specific **S-code and component** when the native capture guard rejects a snapshot. The local diagnostic export records only the bounded failure code and applicable counts, never raw pointers or a memory dump. Details are reset for each request so a previous failure is not shown as a new one.

**This is a diagnostic update, not a confirmed fix for the reported capture failure.** The screenshot establishes that a layout guard rejected the capture, but does not identify which guard or justify weakening it. All existing pointer, ownership, overlap, count, selected-preset and stale-state checks remain. Stage/Restore and game saving are unchanged.
